newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sligos, Axime in alliance talks.
newsitem.headline: Sligos, Axime in alliance talks.

text.p: Two of France's leading computer services companies, Sligos and Axime, said on Monday they were at an advanced stage of talks on a "potential business combination".
Trade in shares of Sligos and Axime, 26.1 percent held by Paribas Affaires Industrielles, a unit of Paribas, were suspended at the companies' request.
The companies said a meeting would be held with employee representatives and their boards of directors on Tuesday and a news conference was set for Wednesday.
The two companies declined any further comment on the announcement.
Sligos is 56.8 percent owned by the state-backed rescue vehicle Consortum de Realisation (CDR) set up to sell off assets owned by struggling French bank Credit Lyonnais.
The CDR said last January it had decided not to sell its stake in Sligos for at least two years to give the company time to complete a restructuring.
Financial analysts have said French computer and software services companies must reach "critical mass" to survive against fierce U.S. competition.
Sligos last month announced it planned to resume a programme of acquisitions broken off in 1994. Sligos, which returned to profit in 1995, has a war chest of 1.5 billion francs and no borrowings.
